## FOXP3

* a member of the fork-winged helix family of transcription factors
* important role in the development and function of naturally occurring CD4-positive/CD25-positive T regulatory cells (Tregs). 

![](./img/foxp3.jpg){width="70%" fig-align="center"}

::: {.tiny-credit}
Josefowicz SZ, Rudensky A. (2009) [Control of regulatory T cell lineage commitment and maintenance. _Immunity_ **30**:616-25](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19464984/)
:::

## HRA

### Kidney renal corpuscle

<iframe data-src="../widgets/ftu-renal-corpuscle.html" width="100%" height="520" style="border:none;"></iframe>

Add web widgets with links to major organs involved

- 1. Intestine (Diarrhea, secretory;  Enteropathy; Ileus)
- 1a. Villi: Villous atrophy seen on biopsy
- 2. Pancreas (Insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, type I)
- 3. Thyroid (hypothyroidism) 
- 4. Immunology (Lymphadenopathy, autoantibodies, autoimmune disorders); 
- 5. autoimmune anemia (also autoimmune low platelets, low neutrophils)
- 6. Nervous System (developmental delay, seizure)
